children: Copper futures continue to hover around all-time highs after a multiday rally driven by concerns over potential U.S. tariffs and supply challenges at key mines worldwide. In early European trading, three-month futures on the London Metal Exchange are down 0.3% to $14,685 a metric ton after settling at $14,728 a ton in the previous session. "Copper therefore needs to hold above $14,600 a ton to preserve the breakout, while a loss of that level could expose the market to a sharper correction given the speed of the recent move," analysts at Sucden Financial say, adding that the narrowing gap between near-term and three-month copper prices suggests that immediate supply pressures are easing, even as the benchmark price remains near record highs. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
